newsitem.title: KENYA: Africans in Great Lakes crisis face famine.
newsitem.headline: Africans in Great Lakes crisis face famine.

text.p: Africans trapped in the refugee and civil war crisis of the Great Lakes region face famine and only urgent action by the international community will end human suffering and loss of lives, the U.N. food agency FAO said.

Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO) said in a report issued in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on Wednesday that fighting in eastern Zaire and an influx of refugees back to Rwanda in end-1996 had created severe food deficits.

"Pockets of famine could develop in eastern Zaire as relief distribution continues to be hampered by hostilities and logistic difficulties," FAO said in a report on the food supply situation and crop prospects in sub-Saharan Africa.

"Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees and sections of the local population are inaccessible to relief agencies and are caught up in the middle of the fighting in the conflict zone. Deaths from malnutrition and disease are already reported.
It added: "Only urgent action by the international community to ensure uninterrupted flow of relief assistance to the trapped refugees will avert further human suffering and loss of life."
FAO said that in Rwanda, the recent sudden influx of more than 1.2 million returning refugees had strained food supplies.
In Burundi, continuing political and social uncertainty and an economic embargo slapped by regional governments to punish a July 25 coup had seriously undermined food production.

FAO said that in Uganda, displacement of local people and Sudanese refugees in the north had resulted in food problems while in Tanzania 280,000 people required food assistance following a poor harvest in 1996.
On Tuesday, Ugandan Deputy Prime Minister Paul Orono Etiang said there was famine in northern and eastern Uganda and that up to 2.1 million people were affected in some 19 districts.
FAO said that a food emergency had already been declared in the eastern and northeastern parts of Kenya after crop failures due to drought and the situation was worsened by rinderest.

"In Somalia, dry weather conditions coupled with continuing insecurity in many areas have led to a tight food supply situation," FAO said. "In Eritrea, another poor harvest has been gathered as a result of insufficient rains."
FAO said bumper harvests had been gathered in Ethiopia and Sudan but food deficits persisted in parts of these nations.

Zairean ADFL rebels have gained a string of victories in eastern Zaire since they launched their war against strongman Mobutu Sese Seko's government in October and in their wake have forced mainly Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire on the move.

On Wednesday, Laurent Kabila's rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), were within range of Kisangani on two axis beyond the northern town of Bafwasende, according to senior regional military sources.

Kisangani is the government army's operational base, the country's third largest city and a key diamond and gold trading centre. Kabila has proclaimed Kisangani as his next target, giving army commanders until March 13 to lay down their arms.
